doc.title: Wendell Brunious interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Armstrong's cousin and Barrett's dreams of Louis
summary: Brunious tells of a babysitter whose cousin was Armstrong; neither has heard him live; Barrett recounts dreams of Armstrong, including Kellso's.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: take them for a cool drink or something. And the lady gets in the car and she says, “You’re a jazz musician, right?” I say, “Yeah.” She says, “You know my cousin played trumpet.” I say, “Really, who is it?” She says, “Louis Armstrong.” Armstrong, man, I got the shakes man.
My cousin played trumpet, oh that’s nice.
You know, you’d think Joe Smooth or somebody you know. Louis Armstrong. That may be enough about Louis even though not enough can be said.
I just want to ask you did you ever hear him in person?
No. I saw him one time but I never really heard him in person.
Yeah, I never did either. I’ve had real vivid dreams about him.

Kind of funny, like hearing him play in these dreams. And he talked to me. Oh it was really weird. And he did it with Jon Kellso too, the young trumpet player in New York. Kellso had a similar dream. Like it makes me cry to think about it. He said he was sitting on a park bench and he saw Louis sitting on this other park bench, and then Louis got up in this dream and walked over the just sat down by him and took his hand and just kind of patted his hand. Like, you know, don’t worry about a thing, everything’s going to be all right. Crazy. Weird.
